items.title: Live: Iran attacks US navy base after US retaliates over helicopter downing
items.description: Iran says it struck the US Navy's Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain with drones following a series of US strikes on Iranian cities along the Strait of Hormuz. Follow live.

items.title: Live: PM 'very worried' about the impact of fresh attacks in Iran war
items.description: Anthony Albanese wants to see a "de-escalation" following the latest strikes in the Middle East. Follow live.

items.title: 'It's an unprecedented matter': Bondi gunman hit with 19 more charges
items.description: Akram is facing charges of murder and committing a terrorist act over the attack at Bondi Beach on 14 December.

items.title: Live: Woolworths set to outsource hundreds of jobs from corporate office
items.description: Supermarket giant Woolworths will begin consulting with its 10,000 corporate workers today, with plans to outsource roles to Asia. The Australian share market has begun its day relatively flat. Follow live.

items.title: Too poor to leave Australia. These people are trapped with no safety net
items.description: A man dies. His body is not noticed for nearly a week. He was invisible to many, like the growing number of homeless Australia wide.

items.title: Protests erupt in Belfast after stabbing attack, homes, cars and bus set on fire
items.description: Protesters hold anti-immigration demonstrations in Northern Ireland and England after a Sudanese man is arrested over a "brutal" knife attack in Belfast.

items.title: Judge throws out appeals over homophobic tweet judgement
items.description: A Federal Court judge has dismissed an appeal against a judgement which ordered New South Wales MP Mark Latham to pay $140,000 to independent MP Alex Greenwich over a homophobic tweet in 2023.

items.title: 'We didn't know how dangerous he was': How Rolf Harris hid in plain sight
items.description: Rolf Harris's conviction for child sexual abuse was shocking to those who saw him as a lovable larrikin. But the people who were abused by him are refusing to stay silent about the impacts of his crimes.

items.title: Why Xi Jinping made an exception to see Kim Jong Un in person
items.description: Xi Jinping and Kim Jong Un's bilateral talks in North Korea were a big departure from the Chinese president's usual diplomacy playbook because, for this first time this year, he was the one travelling abroad to make the meeting happen.

items.title: Thirteen government agencies embroiled in potential data breach
items.description: Thirteen government agencies are now embroiled in an expanding scandal involving potential data breaches prompting calls for an urgent audit amid concerns over national security.

items.title: Musk's xAI hit with class action over power plant's 'inescapable' noise
items.description: US residents say a plant powering data centres has caused them emotional distress and reduced the value of their properties.

items.title: 'It breaks us to have to live like this': Overcrowding in outback NSW
items.description: Delays in maintenance repairs, including mould removal, are forcing families to sleep on mattresses in living rooms, adding to overcrowding pressures in remote homes.

items.title: How police may have inadvertently saved this man from Ivan Milat
items.description: Etched in Steven Clark's memory are the protruding teeth and moustache of the driver he says picked him up as a teenager — a man he now believes was serial killer Ivan Milat.

items.title: Shop worker 'concerned' by security response after knife comment
items.description: A retail worker at Sydney's Broadway Shopping Centre says she was left scared after a man told her he had a knife.

items.title: Why women are at greater risk of intimate partner violence during pregnancy
items.description: Pregnancy is a time of greater autonomy and self-awareness for women. Because domestic violence is about power and control, a pregnancy can challenge that for a person who is using abuse.

items.title: Finding and saving the world's biggest trees before they disappear
items.description: It took a decade for researchers to find the tallest tree in East Asia. Now they know where the 84.1-metre conifer is but the future of its species and other tall trees is dire.

items.title: Calling all budding storytellers living with disability
items.description: If you are an emerging content maker or journalist with disability and have a story to tell, now is your chance to work with the ABC to tell it.

items.title: Is Australia sucking the joy out of childhood?
items.description: The first time Renae Powell waved her eldest child through the primary school gates she felt something was missing: playtime.

items.title: Court rejects appeal to increase sentence of killer driver
items.description: The Court of Appeal has dismissed an appeal to increase the jail term of Christopher Dillon Joannidis, who killed five people in a horrific 2023 crash in Northern Victoria.

items.title: 41yo charged with murder over Wollongong stabbing
items.description: Police have charged a man and say they expect more arrests in relation to the stabbing of Brandon Yates, who was found fatally injured in an apartment in Wollongong in 2025.

items.title: Two people killed in truck, car crash south of Nowra
items.description: The Princes Highway remains closed in both directions as police investigate the cause of the crash.

items.title: Man found dead in Melbourne park had suffered burns, police say
items.description: Police say the man appeared to have suffered burns and was discovered by a passer-by in parkland in Melbourne's east.

items.title: 'Just an absolute tip': Residents frustrated with rise of illegal dumping
items.description: Councils across Melbourne's suburbs are struggling to combat the rise of illegal dumping, despite over $21 million of funding from the Victorian state government.

items.title: Victim-survivors tear up agreement with Catholic church
items.description: Victim-survivors of clergy abuse say negotiations and agreements reached with the Catholic Diocese of Ballarat are now null and void.

items.title: Further $105m federal-state bailout announced for Nyrstar smelters
items.description: The federal, Tasmanian and South Australian governments have contributed to a new funding package for Nyrstar's Hobart and Port Pirie smelters, including money for feasibility studies into modernising and expanding their operations.
